However, when a chicken-pie making machine is installed, their need becomes urgent, and they must devise other means of escape.

She teaches herself for years by going to the library and reading everything she sees. Eventually she convinces her parents to let her go to school, but discovers her special talents are needed to protect the school and her lovely teacher from the evil headmistress.

There she meets a scarecrow, a tin man and a cowardly lion, who join her on a quest to find the all-powerful Wizard of Oz, the only man who can help her get back to Kansas. Before opening the attraction to the public, he invites a top palaeontologist, palaeobotanist, mathematician/theorist, and his two eager grandchildren to experience the park. Their park visit is anything but tranquil as the park's security system breaks down, and the prehistoric creatures break out.

programme.title: Erin Burnett OutFront
programme.desc: It's Erin Burnett's turn to step out front and try to maintain a viable viewer presence for CNN in the weekday news arena. But the former CNBC anchor won't worry about ratings for her hourlong general news program, comparing that burden to "death." Instead, she'll concern herself with translating world events into relevant information for viewers, paying close attention to such topics as the Middle East and women's issues. "I want people to say that our show is smart. I want our show to be authentic", Burnett says in a promo. "I want our show to have courage". Left unsaid, of course, is that she wants her show to have a big audience, too.

programme.title: Smerconish
programme.desc: After serving as an MSNBC contributor and guest-host on the network for four years, TV and radio personality Michael Smerconish believed he was ready to head a show of his own. CNN agreed, and thus was born `Smerconish', an hourlong Saturday morning program that takes after its host's independent views. Using a topical, conversational format, he aims for the TV show to be an extension of his weekday radio broadcast, with free-flowing topics and the ability to discuss issues that strike a chord with the audience. Along the same lines, he thinks it's important to present the content in an engaging manner, free of my-way-or-the-highway ideology. Smerconish, who has a law degree from the University of Pennsylvania, is also a New York Times' best-selling author.

programme.desc: Jason Manford hosts the quiz show where players face a question and pick from a board of six rankable answers. Some answers are good, but only one is unbeatable.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: Engaging conversation about the political issues that matter to you.

programme.title: The Boss
programme.desc: Susan Calman hosts the quiz show where being in control is everything. Who will emerge as the Boss and walk away with the cash? Only the strongest players will survive the game.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: A place in the quarter-final is at stake this week, and the challenges are all about lingerie. Host Sara Pascoe starts the sewers off with a fiddly pattern for a lace underwired bra and matching knicker set. With such small pattern pieces, there is no margin for error, and Patrick and Esmé's eagle eyes will spot every mistake. The Transformation Challenge requires the sewers to take thermal underwear and turn it into daywear.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Living in the depths of the New Guinea rainforest are the spectacular birds of paradise. Filming their bizarre courtship displays is the holy grail of wildlife filmmakers. David Attenborough has been entranced by these birds since he was a boy, and he narrates as a team of New Guinean naturalists embark on a gruelling expedition to try to film ten birds of paradise deep in the heart of the rainforest.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: David Fletcher and Claire Rawle visit Longleat in Wiltshire, where they discover a marble statue and an autograph album that evokes the glamour of a bygone era. Paul Martin discovers how Longleat became a drive-through safari park in 1966.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Richard Osman takes to the host seat for a final week of quizzing before he hands over the baton to a new host next week. He is joined by previous winners Miles Jupp, Cariad Lloyd, Lucy Porter and Kiell Smith-Bynoe, who go head-to-head, testing their general knowledge skills in a variety of fun trivia-based games. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing: It Takes Two
programme.desc: With the first elimination of the series looming, Ellie Taylor chats to the remaining celebs before their next live performances. Also, a panel of former Strictly celebs and pros get an exclusive look at all of the couples' weekend dances for the first time on the Strictly ballroom floor.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Featuring extensive coverage of the day's top national and international news stories, along with explanations about the context and potential aftereffects.

programme.title: BBC Weather
programme.desc: The latest weather forecast.

programme.title: Live: UEFA Nations League Football
programme.desc: Stephen Watson presents full match coverage from the Nations League as Northern Ireland take on Ukraine at Štadión Antona Malatinského in Trnava, Slovakia. Michael O'Neill's team face Ukraine with precious League B points at stake. With promotion the prize for the group winners, can Northern Ireland produce a result to remember? Commentary is by Thomas Kane and Stephen Craigan, with expert analysis from Stuart Dallas, Jim Magilton and David Healy.

programme.title: The Substance
programme.desc: Fading actress Elisabeth Sparkle becomes distressed when her chauvinistic boss fires her from her aerobics show. She soon injects herself with a mysterious serum that promises a younger, better version of herself, but things go horribly wrong.

programme.title: The Wicker Man
programme.desc: Cult mystery thriller in which a police sergeant visits a remote Scottish isle to search for a missing girl but fears for her safety when he finds a community steeped in paganism. The community deny the girl's existence and this, coupled with the sergeant's Christian background, fuels his suspicions - and growing unease - as the investigation continues.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: How cloned and ghost number plates are leaving innocent motorists facing fines, debt collection threats and years of stress.

programme.title: Hey Beautiful: Anatomy of a Romance Scam
programme.desc: Victims meet in person as the true scope of the scam is revealed.

programme.title: This Is BBC TWO
programme.desc: A preview of upcoming programmes from BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Nugget reinvents herself as a comic book hero called Super Nugget, but Pancake is dismissive of her new hobby as defender of the berg. The others persuade him to think again.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When all the vegetables from their garden are stolen, detectives Cosima and Big Lizard investigate all over the neighbourhood, only to return to the scene of the crime.

programme.title: Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Ducklings find a device that creates popcorn after Weasy munches through their supply.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Hoofius's next quest will be his 1000th, so he decides to wait for a really heroic one and insists that his friends quest without him.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: Grizzy and the Lemmings discover a temple dedicated to an ancestral brioche.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is working in a lovely cosy ski lodge, until Frog turns up and ruins everything.

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons: The Series
programme.desc: A tough loss causes Ult to consider what it means to be a Pokémon Trainer.

programme.title: Winx Club: The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: A powerless Bloom joins the Winx as they come to help her save her parents.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: Kenzie organises a sleepover, Olive feels left out, and Melody tries to make amends.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: News magazine keeping young viewers up to date with the latest stories and events happening at home and abroad.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Shini goes behind the scenes with the cast of The Lion King musical.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty is spoiled for choice in an area he knows so well. He views the floral wonders of Britain's Sissinghurst Castle and the vivid palette of impressionist painter Monet at Giverny. Also, he enjoys the quirky individuality of the garden of one of his favourite Belgian designers, and goes to Norway to see what can grow 200 miles north of the Arctic Circle.

programme.title: This Wild Life
programme.desc: With the drought biting hard, food is in short supply and cheeky monkeys are taking over the family's safari camp. With water running short, Saba is struggling to give her guests the experience they expect.

programme.title: Passport to Pimlico
programme.desc: In 1949, a group of Londoners discover an old royal treaty suggesting that Pimlico is legally a part of Burgundy. They declare Pimlico's independence to avoid postwar rationing.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden
programme.desc: Setting out to bring in new livestock, expand the range of produce in his kitchen garden and get some insider tips on veg growing, Marcus heads to one of his old stomping grounds, Gravetye Manor. He explores their grand kitchen garden, before returning to his smallholding to help local farmer Stuart with the hay baling. As he takes on the day-to-day challenges of farming life, gardener Anatoli shows him how to plait his garlic, before Marcus heads to a local artisan to get some of it smoked.

programme.title: Nadiya's Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shares a nifty hack on an old-school quiche, using layers of buttery filo pastry as a speedy base and adorning it with a punchy paprika egg topping. Next, she takes on an American favourite, the snickerdoodle.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: In Bournemouth, Martin warns the buyer to beware, as a huge crack in a three-bedroom house requires urgent attention. In Kent, Jacqui is relieved that it's a brickie who has taken on a challenging renovation.

programme.title: The Cockleshell Heroes
programme.desc: Major Stringer needs to assemble a crack squad of British Royal Marines for a highly unusual mission. Though Captain Thompson is extremely sceptical, he dutifully helps his new superior recruit and train the needed men. Their audacious plan involves transporting a small group of soldiers by submarine to the coast of occupied France, where they will kayak along an estuary into a Nazi shipyard and commit sabotage. Chances for success are very small.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The venue for today is Stockport Town Hall. As usual, hundreds of local visitors visit with their family heirlooms. Paul Martin finds out about the tunnels below the town hall which were used as air raid shelters in World War II.

programme.title: The Bridge at Remagen
programme.desc: World War II film chronicling the tense battle to hold the Ludendorff Bridge at Remagen, the only bridge still standing across the Rhine towards the end of the war. The German officer in charge of the region faces a dilemma - destroy the bridge and strand 50,000 of his own troops on the wrong side of the river, or leave the bridge intact and effectively give up the Fatherland to the advancing Allied forces.
